       2. PROFILE OF LALUK COLLEGE
               Laluk College is a notable institution of higher education in Lakhimpur district of Assam.
       The College was established on the 5th September, 1985 with a noble thought of educating the
       rural backward students irrespective of caste, creed, religion and socio-economic status to
       empower them to face the highly competitive global scenario. The institution silently devoted to
       train young man and women to make able leader in every walk of life with an exalted sense of
       national pride. The College, which is affiliated to Dibrugarh University, offers education in the
       stream of Arts in undergraduate level. The College has 9 (Nine) teaching departments with
       adequate infrastructure. Along with formal education the college offers training in the fields of
       skill development, environment, games and sports, culture, literature and social service.
               Recently, the college has taken up the Choice Based Credit System to make the students
       at par leading universities of the country and to face the challenges globally. The College has
       given due importance to the co-curricular skills of the students. Skill Based courses are
       promoted and employability of the students are given high importance. The institution is keen on
       updating the knowledge and the standard of learning by all means.
               The college was provincialized by the government of Assam on 20-01-2014 w.e.f. 01-01-
       2013. Till now, 11 (eleven) teaching post are sanctioned and 23 (twenty three) more number of
       post are in the process of sanctioning.
               The college is registered under UGC 2(f) and 12 (b). The college is supported financially
       for the infrastructural development by University Grants’ Commission and State Government.
       The college has well equipped indoor stadium, outdoor stadium, women hostel, language lab and
       library constructed out of financial support of UGC. The state government has sanctioned an
       amount of Rs. 1 Cr. for infrastructural development of the college.
       Vision:
           Vision of Laluk College is to empower specially the tribal and minority people and
            students of this area to overcome backwardness through education.
           To provide the rural youth access to higher education and to nurture them to make a
            positive contribution to public life.
           To make the college a centre of academic excellence in the field of higher education.
           To equip the students with the knowledge to enable them to succeed in the highly
            competitive scenario.

                                                       5
     To guide, train and impart value education to the students, so that they become developed
     human resource having the sense of social obligation and national responsibility to be a
     good citizen.
Mission:
    To provide quality education for production of potential human resource irrespective of
       caste, creed, religion and diverse socio-economic status.

       broader society.
      To develop a commitment towards the preservation of environment with a aim towards
       sustainable development.
      To promote management skill of its students and employees using modern tools and

3. SWOC ANALYSIS
Institutional Strength:
        Laluk college has a campus of 69322 sq. mtrs in a pleasant pastoral setting. The college
has dedicated and qualified faculty to enhance learning and research atmosphere and to foster a
spirit of belongingness with a very convivial relationship among the students and the college
staff.
The college maintains strict discipline and the number of working days are always above the
norms stipulated by D.U and UGC.
        The college strictly adheres to the academic calendar. A class diary is maintained by
every department for every teacher recording each and every class taken and other activities
executed.
Promotion of leadership is encouraged among the students through the election of students to the
“Students’ Union” a student representative body.
Almost 80% of students get scholarship from the Government of Assam. A number of curricular,
co-curricular and extra-curricular activities are regularly carried out by NSS, Women Cell and
NGOs of the locality.
        For smooth functioning of the college various responsibilities are shared by committees
like- IQAC, ISMC, CBCS Board, Planning Committee, Anti- ragging Committee, Grievance
Redressal Cell, Women Cell, College Publication Board, College Construction Committee,
Examination Committee, Disciplinary Action Committee, Admission Committee, Academic
Board, Students’ Advisory Committee, NSS Cell, Career Counselling Cell, Purchase Committee,
Gender Sensitization Cell, College Health and Sanitation Cell, Festival Committee, Committee
against Sexual Harassment, Committee for SC/ST, Minority Cell, Internal Compliant
Committee, OBC Committee, Waste Management Cell, College Research and Development
Committee and College Canteen Committee.
        The college organizes annual orientation programme, workshops, seminar and meeting
with external resource persons. The college offer free internet facilities, LCD screens,

                                               6
 computers, projectors etc. Fee concession is given to poor and needy students. There is an active
parent-Teacher association in the college. The college has four smart classrooms, active NSS
and Women Cell. The college has Biometric system of attendance for Staff along with CC
Camera in all the class rooms, office and surrounding college premises including entry and exit
point of the college. The college has a well equipped Women’s hostel for the benefit of
outstation girl students. The college has sufficient space in terms of classroom, conference
rooms, library etc.
Institutional Weakness:
         Most of the students are from poor and rural background and they lack communication
skill, they are first generation learners.
         Only 11 out of 34 faculty posts have been sanctioned. It provides a sense of disparity
among the teaching faculty disturbing the team work environment. It continues to increase the
workload and administrative responsibilities of the sanctioned faculty. The prolonged process of
provincialization affects the teaching-learning process.
         The college has limited focus on research activities due to lack of platform for research,
very few numbers of sanctioned posts and financial insecurity of non-sanctioned faculty. There
are only six teachers having Ph.D. and nine teachers having M.Phil. It has only one MRP.
Average publications by the teachers are low. The placement record of the college is poor.
Progression of students as to higher education on an average is about 20% only. Participation of
alumnae in the overall development of the college is minimal.
Institutional Opportunity:
    Most of the students are from marginalized society with poor income. The college
     provided all expenditure related to study in the college.
    Nearly 90% of students are from socially deprived, represents ST, SC, OBC and
     Minorities. The institution offers a great opportunity for overall progress of such
     students.
    Improving teacher quality by virtue of making them to pursue Ph.D. and attend seminar,
     workshop, conference, write book and research papers.
    The college has a well arranged play ground and thereby the institution offer a great
     opportunity to its students to develop themselves in the field of Games and Sports.
    Making the whole campus Wi-Fi enabled.
    Provide proper coaching for the various competitive examinations is an important
     opportunity available in the college.
Institutional Challenge:
    Being an affiliated institution and rapid change of the curriculum from old course (1+1+1) to
new (Semester), and again to CBCS within five to six years, it is a challenge to integrate the
rapidly changing scenario and to utilize internal resources for better management.
     To make the students communicate in English.
     To produce 100% result.
     Students Progress in terms of higher education and employment.
     Encouraging faculty to stay focused of research.
     Complete digitalization of college library.
     Promoting creative and innovative spirit among the students and teachers.

 6. CRITERIA WISE SUMMARY
A. Curricular Aspects:
       Laluk College ensures effective curriculum delivery adhering to the academic calendar of
its affiliating Dibrugarh University. However, to meet the local requirement and for the
betterment of the student community, the academic board and IQAC of the college carries out
minor modification in the curriculum best suited to the students. After the decision of the
academic board and IQAC, the departments also fame its academic calendar with the distribution
of course among the teachers and framing time table and topic for seminar, workshop, home
assignment and group discussions. During the progress of the course continuous comprehensive
evaluation system is also implemented along with demarcation of teachers for ICT enabled and
Digital classes taking support of YouTube and different e-sources for effective delivery of the
course curriculum. Along with normal course curriculum, students are involved for departmental
quizzes, paper presentations, projects, term papers, educational tours, field trips and industrial
visits. Proctorial system of learning is also used in the college. College has central library and
departmental libraries to provide back up for in-depth knowledge of the students and staff. There
is provision for internal examinations for evaluation of the students through class test and
Sessional examination test for monitoring of the development of the students. Low performing
students are given remedial coaching for their upliftment. The College has introduced one
diploma course in computer application in the year 2015-16 with enrolment of 87 students and
one certificate course has been introduced in the session 2016-17 by Gandhian Studies Centre
with enrolment of 93 students. The college has been offering flexibility in its course curriculum
of elective courses under semester system in the year 2011-12 and Choice Based Credit System
has been introduced in 2019-20. The college imparts teaching in Environmental Studies, two
(02) Skill Based Programmes having 4 full-fledged papers of hundred marks with practical and
field survey in each programme and it has introduced programme on gender equality.

B. Teaching-learning and Evaluation:
       Laluk College caters for academic requirement for vast area with a great demand of
seats. Therefore, the Academic Board of the College decides on number of seats with approval
from affiliating Dibrugarh University. The enrolment of 353 students against sanctioned seat of
360 in 2014-15, 348 against 350 in 2015-16, 353 against 360 in 2016-17, 247 against 330 in
2017-18 and 345 against 350 in 2018-19, keeping requisite numbers of seats for reserved
category. However, the seats are offered in open category after non-fill up by reserved category.
The students are subjected to regular attendance of classes, frequent class tests, scheduled
                                                9
 Sessional Examinations, departmental Seminars, workshops, quizzical, Group Discussions, Field
trips, etc. and remedial classes for low performing students.

       Academic activities are planned by Academic Board and executed in close cognizance of
IQAC, with activity report submission to IQAC. The college conducts all the examinations
adhering to the norms and practices formulated by the university. The college plans for ICT
enabled and digital classroom teaching. 25 Nos. of teachers are efficient to take classes with e-
learning resources. The students are supported by teachers keeping in touch with all the time in
mentor-mentee system. Out of 34 teachers, 30 Nos. of teachers are mentoring the students with
close relation and personal care.

       The students’ performance is evaluated for internal assessment by the departments of the
college. 20% weightage of the final marks are given from internal assessment comprising 5%
regularity of attendance, 10% from Sessional Examinations, and 5% from performance in
Workshop, Seminar, Group Discussion, etc. and it is transparent and notified to the students.
College has Grievances Redressal Cell, Internal Compliant committee and many other
committees to address the issues faced by the students. The students are trained for development
of personality, skill and competitive preparedness.

C. Research, Innovations and Extension:
       Laluk College has 34 numbers of full time teachers to teach. It has a beautiful eco-system
with innovation pisciculture. It has created employment important for the youths as well as
revenue for the college. Along with this the pond of the college is serving the purpose of natural
reservoir of harvested rain water of the college. It has created an ecological balanced
environment in the midst of the college. The college has a set of Ethics to prevent malpractices
and plagiarism. It has a publication board and it supports in the publication of 15 numbers in
2014-15, 27 numbers in 2015-16, 20 in 2016-17, 4 in 2017-18 and 2 in 2018-19. One of the
teachers of Economics department also completed one Minor Research Project under the
sponsorship of UGC. The college has executed various extension activities though NSS, IQAC,
different departments, Women Cell, various Cells and Committees on social, environment and
educational tour, Swachcha Bharat, AIDS awareness, gender issues etc. with the participation of
627 students in 2016-17, 498 in 207-18 and 15 in 2018-19. The college has collaboration with
Nowboicha College for exchange of students and faculty w.e.f. 2014-15. It has collaboration
with two NGOs’ namely MARUF NGO and Laluk Sammanay Kendra for various awareness
programmes, social activities and computer education respectively. The college has served


                                                10
 society or community as its responsibility towards it through the extension activities executed by
various forums of the college.

D. Infrastructure and Learning Resources:
        The college has 18 (eighteen) fully functional classrooms and 02 (two) halls with 09
(nine) departmental rooms. Among these classrooms, there are 04 (four) ICT enable classroom
and 02 (two) digital classrooms. The college has a central library with online facilities for
teachers and students. It has installed 2 KVA solar power panels and 16 KVA generator for
uninterrupted power supply. The college has set up facilities for sports and games inside the
campus in the form of indoor and outdoor stadium. There is positive environment of art and
culture in the college. Annual college programme annual competition, college foundation day,
freshmen social, etc are celebrated with cultural activities. The college has various musical
instruments like Harmonium, table, flute, guitar, Dhol, Taal, Pepa, Dholki, Gagana, etc. The
college is equipped with fire safety devices. The college library has a collection of 5, 700 books
and journals comprising about 100 rare books. The college has sufficient infrastructure for
classroom, library, women hostel, departmental rooms, administrative block, stadium, etc. These
are well furnished with furniture and other necessary items.

E. Student Support and Progression:
       Laluk College provides adequate support for the progress of students either in form of
donation of books. 140 numbers of students in 2014-15, 100 in 2015-16 and 9 students in 2018-
19 have been benefitted by scholarship and freeship provided by government of Assam. The
college has introduced capability enhancement and development schemes on competitive
examinations, career counselling, remedial coaching, language lab, Yoga and meditation and
personal counselling and guidance for competitive examination have benefitted numerous
students with participation of 165 students in 2015-16., 152 in 2016-17 and 150 in 2017-18 in
the programmes. Being in the non industrial rural area without having any absorption facility,
still it has placement of good numbers of students who have cleared state government
examination (TET) with participation of 9 students in 204-15, 12 in 2015-16, 14 in 2016-17, 31
in 2017-18 and 18 in 2018-19.There are 3 students in 2017-18 and 2 students in 2018-19 to
receive medals participating in national level programmes. The college has provided a platform
to the students in the form of students’ union and participation of the students in Students’
Advisory Committee. It has been providing facilities for sports and cultural activities. It has
active Alumni Association since 2014. The association has been actively participating in the
development of the college. It collects donation from members and others to help monetarily in
procuring items in the college and departments. It has a schedule meeting twice a year.



                                               11
 F. Governance, Leadership and Management:
       Laluk College was established to empower the youth through quality education and
transforms the society with the development of human resources.

       The united efforts of Governing Body as management, Principal and non-teaching staff
and faculty members develop and implement quality policy. Involvement of all stake holders
including parents towards development of the Students and creating viable academic
environment, IQAC of the college takes feedback from various stakeholders for taking
corrective strategy. The college practices decentralized and participative management. Assam
Government, affiliating University and GB, being higher authority for the college, activities of
the college are executed by Committees, Cells and Departments. The institution frames quality
policy, developed, driven, deployed and reviewed through discussion in the governing Body,
Academic Board, Staff and IQAC meeting. The college conducts Academic Administrative
Audit, encourages participation in the research work, conducts community development
activities, career counselling, remedial coaching, ICT enable facilities, refresher courses and
support of sufficient numbers of classrooms, departments, rooms and other needs of the students.
The college has Governing Body as per the norms given by the Government of Assam and
affiliating university and it executes academic and administrative plans and policies with the
help of 28 numbers of committees and cells available in the college. The college has been taking
various effective welfare measures for teaching and non-teaching staff. It has been regularly
deputing its staff members for attending training, seminar, workshop, career development
programme, orientation course, faculty development programmes and refresher courses. The
college has been supporting its non-sanctioned staff for their children’s education and with the
formation of welfare fund to help the needy. The college has been organizing professional
development training programme for teaching and non-teaching staff since 2014. The college
has a mechanism to monitor the activities of the faculty members and to evaluate the
performance through Performance Appraisal System. The college has IQAC to record the
additional activities, researches, seminar, workshop, publication and research work undertaken
by the faculty members. The college has class diary in each department for keeping record of the
academic activity and social or community activities done by the individual.

G. Institutional Values and Best Practices:
       Laluk College has been conducting Gender Equity programmes since 2014. It has
adequate facility for safety and security, counselling and separate common room for male and
female students. For making the premise safe, the classrooms, library, office room, common

                                               12
 rooms, canteen, Laboratories, indoor stadium, entry and exit and the whole premise of the
college have been put under CCTV surveillance. College has the system of counselling through
mentor and mentee, internal compliance committee, disciplinary action committee, Grievances
Redressal Committee, Women Cell, Committee against Sexual Harassment, Gender sensitization
Cell, Committees for ST/SC, OBC and minority Cell, Anti-Ragging Committee. etc. The college
has adequate, solid, liquid and e-waste management system. NSS of the college is given
responsibility to manage the waste. The college has effective rain water harvesting for
conservation of rain water. The water is used for toiletries, pisciculture and gardening. The
college uses green practices using bicycle, public transport and making the campus plastic free
and also making the landscape green with plantation. The college has physical facilities like
ramps and restrooms and even wheel chair for the differently abled students. The college has
appointed scribes for examinations for the blinds. The college celebrate festivals like national
voters day, international women’s day, republic day, world environment day, NSS day,
international Yoga day, Teachers’ day, Hindi Divas, Swachhta Pakhwada, Gandhi Jayanti,
Children’s day and national education day in a regular basis. The institution maintains financial
and administrative transparency. The college implements best practice through NSS and other
committees for the betterment of the student communities and society.

7. LIBRARY
        The college library was introduced as automated in our college in 2019 after purchase the
SOUL Version 2.0 FE software from INFLIBNET (an autonomous body of UGC). After the
completion of computerized data entry process is completed. For this circulation system the
library uses Bar code printer and scanner for fast transaction of the library resources. Bar coding
of documents was done and bar coded library membership cards were also introduced in 2018.
Periodically list of books and reminders are generated in an automated way. Acquisition of serial,
maintaining issue records, sending reminders of missing issues, generating binding lists, etc. are
also being done in an automated in manner. User education programmes are also organized from
time to time for students and faculty (generally in August-September every year to make best
from these provisions. Library services like circulation, fine calculation, defaulter list
preparation, OPAC (Online Public Access Catalog) etc. are functioning in our college library.
The OPAC is made available to the users to identify the status of availability of documents in the
library. The Library has been connected with internet connectivity for accessing e-resources. The
library has also Digital Database. Laluk College Library is at the 1 st floor at the building adjacent
to Indoor stadium of the College. Library is equipped with 40 seating capacity. Library is fully
automated with Wi-Fi. Moreover there are provided computers for students. The size of Library
is 2100 square feet by its area. The college library is connected to N-LIST INFLIBNET for e-
resources.
